reading.body:
CyrusOne Houston is the largest published data center campus in Texas by disclosed IT load, holding 84 MW across HOU3 and HOU4, 18 percent of the state's 475 MW of published capacity.

At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this 84 MW translates to roughly 2,100 racks; at 10 kW per GPU, it could support about 8,400 high-end accelerators if fully allocated to GPU compute. That scale is enough to matter for AI training clusters, but the campus's Green Globes certification speaks to energy efficiency operations, not AI workload specificity.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, and the vast majority publish no power figures, so the full state capacity is unknown. Whether this campus's grid connection supports sustained AI training loads is not published, leaving its true share of AI-ready power supply in Texas undetermined.
